dialogue.content: （こんばんは！短い間ですが本日はよろしくお願い致します。定刻になったら始めさせていただきます。）
dialogue.English: (Good evening! It will be a short session, but I look forward to working with you today. We will begin at the scheduled time.)

dialogue.content: 宜しくお願いします！
dialogue.English: I look forward to it!

dialogue.content: こんにちは、相談員です。今日はご相談ありがとうございます。最初に、年齢、性別、相談内容を教えて下さい。
dialogue.English: Hello, I’m the counselor. Thank you for reaching out today. To begin, could you tell me your age, gender, and what you’d like to discuss?

dialogue.content: 40代　女性です。子供の育て方で悩んでます
dialogue.English: I’m a woman in my 40s. I’m struggling with how to raise my child.

dialogue.content: 教えていただきありがとうございます。子供の育て方でお悩みなんですね。詳しく教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Thank you for sharing that. So, you're concerned about how to raise your child. Could you please tell me more about it?

dialogue.content: 学校に行きたがらず、タブレットばかりみています。取り上げると怒り、この前は物を投げてテレビを壊しました
dialogue.English: My child doesn't want to go to school and is always on their tablet. If I take it away, they get angry, and the other day they threw something and broke the TV.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。それは心配になりますね。お子さんはおいくつなんですか？
dialogue.English: I see. That must be very worrying. How old is your child?

dialogue.content: 小学生でもうすぐ6年です
dialogue.English: They're in elementary school, about to start 6th grade.

dialogue.content: 6年生なんですね。いつからそのような状態が続いているんですか？
dialogue.English: A 6th grader, I see. How long has this been going on?

dialogue.content: 学校を嫌がるようになったのは最近ですが癇癪は小さい頃からありました私に暴力を振るうときもあります
dialogue.English: The refusal to go to school started recently, but the temper tantrums have been happening since they were little. Sometimes they become physically violent toward me.

dialogue.content: 癇癪は小さい頃からあったんですね。暴力振るわれたときはどのような対応されたんですか？
dialogue.English: So the tantrums have been there since early childhood. How have you responded when they were violent?

dialogue.content: わたしもやり返したりしましたがもう大きくなってきたので怒らせないようにしています
dialogue.English: I used to fight back, but now that they're getting bigger, I try not to provoke them.

dialogue.content: 大きくなった子供の暴力は怖いですよね。家族構成を教えていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Violence from a child who is getting bigger can be frightening, can't it? Could you tell me about your family?

dialogue.content: 夫と私と子供、三人です
dialogue.English: It’s my husband, me, and our child—the three of us.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。パートナーの方にも暴力を振るうことはありますか？
dialogue.English: Thank you. Are they ever violent towards your partner?

dialogue.content: 無いです。彼は怒らないので
dialogue.English: No. He doesn’t get angry.

dialogue.content: なるほどですね。注意をされたら怒るという感じなんですね。お子さんのことを思って注意していることが、怒りになって返ってくるのは悲しいですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. It sounds like they get angry when they’re corrected. It’s painful when the guidance you offer out of care for your child comes back as anger, isn’t it?

dialogue.content: はい嫌いになりそうです
dialogue.English: Yes, I feel like I’m starting to dislike them.

dialogue.content: お母さんとして、息子の幸せを思って怖い中注意されてたことがとても息子さん思いなお母さんだと感じます。
dialogue.English: As a mother, correcting your son for his own happiness, even though it's frightening for you, shows me that you are a very caring mother who thinks deeply about her son.

dialogue.content: あっ女の子です、、
dialogue.English: Oh, she’s a girl...

dialogue.content: すいません。大変失礼しました。娘さんですね。
dialogue.English: I'm so sorry. That was very rude of me. Your daughter, then.

dialogue.content: 暴力って書いたからですよね女の子なのに癇癪持ちです
dialogue.English: It's because I wrote "violence," isn't it? Even though she's a girl, she has severe tantrums.

dialogue.content: 女の子も癇癪持ちの子はよくありますよ。お母さんの思いとしてどうなってくれたらいいとかありますか？
dialogue.English: It's quite common for girls to have tantrums, too. As her mother, what are your hopes for how you'd like things to be?

dialogue.content: 癇癪のことよりも学校へ行ってほしい学歴も大切ですよねあの子の将来が不安です
dialogue.English: More than the tantrums, I want her to go to school. Her education is important, right? I'm worried about her future.

dialogue.content: 将来のためにも学校に行ってほしいという思いなんですね。どんな風な将来になってほしいですか？
dialogue.English: So you want her to go to school for the sake of her future. What kind of future do you hope for her?

dialogue.content: 最低、高校はでて資格などをとって、自立できるまでが親の責任だと、、
dialogue.English: At the very least, I want her to finish high school, get some certifications, and become independent—I feel that’s our responsibility as parents...

dialogue.content: そこまで娘さんのことを思われているのは娘さんにとってとても素敵なお母さんですよね。娘さんとは普段お話とかされたりしますか？
dialogue.English: To think that much about your daughter's future means you're a wonderful mother to her. Do you usually talk with your daughter?

dialogue.content: します期限のいい時は普通に話します
dialogue.English: Yes, we do. When she’s in a good mood, we talk normally.

dialogue.content: ごめんなさい機嫌でした
dialogue.English: Sorry, I meant "mood."

dialogue.content: 普段お話されるんですね。学校に行きたくない理由とかは聞いたことありますか？
dialogue.English: So you do talk regularly. Have you ever asked her why she doesn't want to go to school?

dialogue.content: 意地悪な子がいると言っています
dialogue.English: She says there's a mean kid.

dialogue.content: どんな意地悪されるとか言っていましたか？
dialogue.English: Did she say what kind of mean things they do?

dialogue.content: ものを隠されたり私の服がダサいとかブスだとか言われたと、、その子のお母さんはとてもおしゃれで美人のママさんです
dialogue.English: She said her belongings were hidden, and she was told things like ‘your clothes are tacky’ and ‘you’re ugly.’ That girl’s mother is a very stylish and beautiful mom.

dialogue.content: そうだったんですね。その意地悪が原因で学校に行きたくないって抵抗が暴力という表現になってしまっているんですかね？
dialogue.English: I see. So, is it possible that her resistance to going to school because of that bullying is being expressed through violence?

dialogue.content: やり返してこいっていったんですけどね
dialogue.English: I told her to fight back, though.

dialogue.content: それを言ったら娘さんはなんと言ってましたか？
dialogue.English: When you said that, what did your daughter say?

dialogue.content: 外では我慢してるみたいです。何を言われてもで、家ではやりたい放題です
dialogue.English: It seems she holds it in when she's outside, no matter what is said to her. But at home, she does whatever she wants.

dialogue.content: 外でできない分、お家でやりたい放題になってしまっているんですね。なにか娘さんの気持ちの発散方法とかほかになにか聞いたことありますか？
dialogue.English: So she's letting it all out at home because she can't do it outside. Have you heard of any other ways your daughter vents her feelings?

dialogue.content: 最近は化粧ばかりして
dialogue.English: Lately, she's been doing her makeup all the time.

dialogue.content: 楽しいみたいです
dialogue.English: She seems to enjoy it.

dialogue.content: お化粧が楽しいんですね。もう少しお話を聞かせていただきたいところではありますが、そろそろお時間になります。本日お話してみていかがでしたか？
dialogue.English: So she enjoys doing makeup. I would love to hear more, but we're almost out of time. How was it talking about this today?

dialogue.content: 学校に行ってほしいという想いはまだありますが子供も我慢していたんだと少し冷静になれましたありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: I still want her to go to school, but I was able to calm down a bit, realizing that she has been holding a lot in too. Thank you.

dialogue.content: お子さんもお子さんなりの抵抗だったのかもしれませんね。お話を聞かせていただいて、娘さんの幸せを真剣に思われているお母さんだからこその悩みだと思います。その思いがきっと娘さんにも伝わっていると思います。本日はご相談いただきありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: It may have been her own way of resisting. From what you’ve shared, I can tell these concerns come from how deeply you care about your daughter’s happiness. I’m sure that feeling is reaching her as well. Thank you very much for consulting with me today.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございました
dialogue.English: Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: それでは失礼致します。
dialogue.English: Then I'll be concluding our session.

dialogue.content: （本日はクライアント役ありがとうございました。また機会がありましたらよろしくお願い致します。）
dialogue.English: (Thank you for playing the role of the client today. I look forward to working with you again if we have the chance.)

dialogue.content: こちらこそありがとうございました。是非またよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Thank you as well. I'd definitely like to do this again.

dialogue.content: （それでは失礼致します。）
dialogue.English: (Then, I'll take my leave.)
